citation.title: Machine-learning-assisted multiscale topology optimization of functionally graded superimposed lattice structures
citation.authors: Prashant Kumar Gupta, Jonathan Stollberg, Dominik Schillinger, Mohammad Ashraf Iqbal
citation.version_coded: arXiv v1 (28 Aug 2026), HTML full text incl. Appendix A; v1 is the only version; no version of record found (web search 2026-09-24)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Two offline-trained networks, one for stiffness and one for density, stand in for unit-cell homogenization at every MMA lattice iteration, framed as removing the homogenization cost that limits graded-lattice multiscale TO; nothing is timed or run classically.
claim.key_phrase: The trained stiffness and density surrogates replace repeated online homogenization
claim.location: abstract, sentences 1 and 10; restated in Sec. 4.4 para 1 and Sec. 5 para 2
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No times, FE-solve counts or speed-up factors are reported anywhere (full text read, incl. Appendix A).
claim.alternatives: (1) Sec. 4.4 para 2: qualitative contrast with plain single-scale SIMP output, which the framework extends with lattice-parameter and relative-density fields; an output-richness claim, not speed or quality. (2) Sec. 5 para 2: the conclusion repeats that the surrogates avoid online unit-cell homogenization. No quantitative comparison with any classical method exists in the article.

baseline.classical_method: Implicit comparator only: multiscale lattice optimization with repeated online computational homogenization, never run. The pipeline itself uses SIMP with OC and a sensitivity filter for the macroscale stage (Sec. 3, Table 2) and MMA with the NN surrogates for the lattice stage (Sec. 4.2).
baseline.implementation: No classical baseline implementation. Surrogates in Julia/Flux (Sec. 2.3); training data from an in-house homogenization code with Gmsh meshes and Abaqus cubic Euler-Bernoulli beam elements (Sec. 2.2); MMA from an open-source implementation, ref. [40] (Sec. 4.2).
baseline.problem_size: 3D MBB beam, domain 20 × 5 × 5, 60 × 15 × 15 = 13,500 first-order hexahedral elements (Sec. 4.1)
baseline.classical_iterations: No classical run. Pipeline stopping rules: SIMP stage stops on windowed relative compliance change with N = 5 and tolerance 10^-3 (Eq. 25, Table 2); lattice stage stopped after 32 iterations at tolerance 10^-3 (Eq. 29, Sec. 4.2).
baseline.training_time: not stated; stiffness network 50,000 epochs with AMSGrad, learning rate 3 × 10^-3 (Sec. 2.3); density network 500 epochs with Adam, learning rate 1 × 10^-3 (Sec. 2.4)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated as time or compute; 1,926 homogenized stiffness samples (Sec. 2.3), each from six unit-strain beam-FE load cases (Eq. 8, Sec. 2.2), and 1,500 Monte Carlo relative-density estimates using 500 to 2,000 points each (Sec. 2.4, Table 1)
baseline.quality_metric: Surrogate accuracy on held-out data: stiffness R^2 = 0.974, relative L2 error 9.2 %, RMSE 0.32 on 386 test samples (Sec. 2.3, Fig. 6); density R^2 = 0.965, relative L2 error 8.0 %, RMSE 1.1 × 10^-2 on 300 test samples (Sec. 2.4, Fig. 10). Design quality only as the surrogate-based compliance history: final compliance 1.46 times the initial value after 32 iterations (Sec. 4.2, Fig. 13).
baseline.quality_gap: not stated; the surrogate-based design is never compared with a directly homogenized or classical multiscale design (Sec. 4.4 defers this check)

R1.evidence: Abstract, Sec. 4.4, Sec. 5: the cost-avoidance claim against online homogenization has no design-quality comparison with any classical multiscale result. Sec. 4.4 leaves for future work any check of the final design by direct homogenization.

R2.evidence: Full text: no classical baseline is executed or timed. The comparator appears only as the avoided cost (abstract sentence 1; Sec. 1 para 3), so solver efficiency and hardware cannot be judged. [judgment] pass would also be defensible.

R3.evidence: Sec. 2.3-2.4, Table 1: offline effort is given only as counts (1,926 stiffness and 1,500 density samples; 50,000 and 500 epochs). No data-generation or training time and no break-even against the online homogenizations avoided. [judgment] fail is arguable if counts are not accepted as cost.

R4.evidence: Sec. 4.2-4.4, Figs. 13-14: compliance and relative density of the returned lattice design come from the NN surrogates inside the FE model. No direct homogenization, Monte Carlo density check or full-lattice FE of the final design. Sec. 4.4 calls the fields approximate (relative L2 error of the stiffness factors 9.2 %, and 13.0 % for G33; Sec. 2.3).

reporting.n_test_cases: 1 optimization benchmark (3D MBB beam, Sec. 4.1); surrogate hold-out sets of 386 stiffness samples (Sec. 2.3) and 300 density samples (Sec. 2.4)

notes: Borderline include: the only comparison with a classical method is a qualitative cost-avoidance claim; the article reports no timing, no solve-count comparison and no classical run. If the verifier judges that no comparison is made, recode as exclude with FT-no-classical-comparison. Data availability section: data and code from the corresponding author on reasonable request. The authors declare LLM-assisted language editing. Figure images were not inspected; coding uses text, tables and captions.
